headline: Supply chains struggle. Budgets expand. Companies pivot.
deck: This week, space supply chains and funding strategies are under scrutiny as companies adapt to shifting demands.

stories.head: U.S. space supply chains lean on China
stories.body: A recent report highlights that U.S. space supply chains are heavily reliant on Chinese manufacturing and Taiwanese semiconductors, raising concerns about national security and supply chain resilience. This reliance has implications for companies like SpaceX and Boeing, which may face disruptions if geopolitical tensions escalate. As the industry pushes for more domestic production, the question remains: can they scale up fast enough?
stories.soWhat: If the supply chain is a house of cards, it’s starting to look like a game of Jenga.

stories.head: FY27 budget adds $1.4B for space resilience
stories.body: The FY27 budget markup includes a significant $1.4 billion increase for space resilience initiatives, reflecting a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space assets. This funding surge could benefit companies like True Anomaly and Ursa Major, which are positioned to support national security missions. The government seems to be finally acknowledging that space is not just a nice-to-have.
stories.soWhat: It’s about time the budget reflects the reality that space isn’t going away; it’s just getting more crowded.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the Department of Defense has successfully passed its critical design review, which is a necessary step toward eventual production. The company aims to leverage this milestone to secure further contracts, especially as the DoD looks to diversify its space capabilities. However, the real challenge lies in turning this approval into an actual launch.
stories.soWhat: Passing a review is like getting a parking ticket; it’s a step forward, but you still might not get where you want to go.

watchlist.title: Watch for True Anomaly's next steps
watchlist.body: With a fresh $190M Series C, True Anomaly’s moves could reshape co-orbital security strategies.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's launch plans
watchlist.body: Following the design review, the timeline for Dream Chaser's launch will be critical to monitor.

watchlist.title: Implications of GPS jamming resurgence
watchlist.body: The return of GPS jamming in the Eastern Med could impact military operations and insurance assessments.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension impact
watchlist.body: The $480M extension for the TITAN program could signal further consolidation in ground station capabilities.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
